content.text:
Review target: `https://github.com/william-coronado/syncd/pull/7`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

{"baseRefName":"main","body":"Confine scans, copies, moves, trash operations and directory changes to sync roots. Reject symlink ancestors and replaced roots, including parent swaps during execution. Refuse case-insensitive path aliases before planning changes, including directory and manifest aliases.

Retain full scan timestamps and verify destination hashes before robust overwrites or deletes. Use a shared canonical, unordered root-pair lock for sync and watch, while preserving their separate state databases.

Add regression coverage, replace racy fsnotify test injections with an owned error channel, document the safety behavior and lock migration, and include the requested Claude/Codex Entire hook settings.

Validation: go test ./..., go test -race ./..., go vet ./..., go build ./...; Linux amd64 and Darwin arm64 cross-builds.


Entire-Checkpoint: 01M7E6WKVPKAAYM5JH6WA7FVZ6

## Summary by Sourcery

Harden synchronization against symlink escapes, concurrent filesystem changes, ambiguous paths, and overlapping sync processes.

New Features:
- Confine synchronization scans and filesystem mutations to pinned sync roots, rejecting symlink escapes and unsafe root replacements.
- Detect and refuse case-insensitive path aliases across files, directories, skipped entries, and manifests.
- Use identity, full-precision timestamps, and content hashes to guard overwrites, moves, trash operations, and deletes against concurrent changes.
- Coordinate sync and watch processes with a shared canonical, order-independent root-pair lock while retaining separate state databases.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent reconciliation from following symlinked ancestors or writing through roots and parent directories replaced during execution.
- Preserve concurrent replacements and retain displaced data for recovery instead of overwriting or deleting newer entries.
- Replace racy fsnotify test injections with an application-owned error channel.

Enhancements:
- Add root-confined filesystem primitives, exclusive publication, holding-directory recovery, and safer cross-device trash handling.
- Retain full scan timestamps and improve scoped reconciliation safety checks.

Documentation:
- Document filesystem safety guarantees, case-alias handling, recovery behavior, and root-pair lock migration.

Tests:
- Add regression coverage for symlink escapes, root swaps, case aliases, timestamp-preserving edits, exclusive publication, trash safety, and shared sync/watch locking.

findings.short_summary: Case-only rename permanently wedges sync
findings.summary: CheckCaseAliases folds manifest/baseline paths together with both scans, so a case-only rename (or deleting `Foo` and creating `foo`) is refused before planning, and because the manifest is never updated the refusal repeats forever.
findings.failure_scenario: User renames `Report.pdf` → `report.pdf` locally. Manifest holds `Report.pdf`, local scan has `report.pdf`, remote still has `Report.pdf` → `case-insensitive path collision` on every scoped cycle, remote poll and deep scan. Renaming the remote too doesn't help (manifest still has the old spelling); the only escape is reverting the rename or deleting the manifest DB. Same for fast two-way via `prev` baseline (sync_once.go:359).

findings.short_summary: Holding dirs abort other clients' scans
findings.summary: Transient `.syncd-hold-*` directories are created inside the synced tree (including on the shared remote), and the scanner hard-fails on them before the ignore matcher runs, so any concurrent scan by another machine — or any leftover from a failed post-publish check — aborts the whole cycle.
findings.failure_scenario: Machine A overwrites/deletes a file on the NAS (claimEntry makes `.syncd-hold-…` in that remote dir). Machine B's remote poll walks the share at that moment → `unfinished sync operation` → whole RunRobustOnce fails. Separately, if `check(claimed, leaf)` after publish fails (e.g. a transient SMB read error while hashing), the holding dir is left behind and every cycle on every client errors until someone cleans it up by hand. claim.go's comment says the name is 'excluded from reconciliation', but it isn't.

findings.short_summary: Overwrites/deletes need RENAME_EXCL or hard links
findings.summary: Every robust overwrite, every delete (including network deletes that used to be a plain unlink), and every exclusive publish now requires the destination FS to support RENAME_EXCL/RENAME_NOREPLACE or hard links; on mounts with neither, all such operations fail.
findings.failure_scenario: On a macOS smbfs mount where renameatx_np(RENAME_EXCL) returns ENOTSUP/EINVAL and linkat isn't supported (SMB without unix extensions), checkExclusivePublish fails → RemoveFrom/CopyChecked return 'filesystem cannot safely restore', and absent-dest uploads fail in publishExclusive. Remote deletes, overwrites and new uploads to the NAS all stop. Needs verification against the real Synology mount.

findings.short_summary: mtime now set before fsync/close
findings.summary: The preserved mtime is applied before `tmp.Sync()`/`tmp.Close()`, whereas the old code deliberately set it after closing; on network filesystems, cached writes flushed at fsync/close can bump the mtime to 'now'.
findings.failure_scenario: Download/upload to smbfs or NFS: the write is buffered, UtimesNanoAt sets the source mtime, then Sync flushes data and the server updates last-write time. Destination mtime ≠ source mtime, so the fast reconciler (size+mtime) re-copies forever, and robust HashIfChanged re-hashes every cycle.

findings.short_summary: Scoped cycle loads full manifest names per batch
findings.summary: RunRobustScoped now calls `Repo.LoadNames` (a full `file_manifest` table scan) and `dirRepo.LoadAll` on every fsnotify batch, and CheckScopedCaseAliases walks every baseline name and its ancestors, undoing the 'scoped cost scales with the batch' design noted a few lines above.
findings.failure_scenario: A 500k-file tree: every single-file save now loads 500k paths from SQLite and does ~500k×depth map lookups before reconciling one path — the hot path scales with the tree again.

findings.short_summary: Destination re-hashed up to 3× per action
findings.summary: checkObserved hashes the full destination content on every call, and copyBetween calls it up to three times per overwrite (claim, after preserve, after publish); deletes also now fully read each target, and the EXDEV trash path hashes 3–4×.
findings.failure_scenario: Overwriting a 2 GB file on the NAS reads it 3 times over SMB (~80 s at 76 MB/s) before the new copy lands; a remote mirror deletion of 1000 large files reads every one of them in full just to delete it. Hashing once after claim plus a cheap identity/size/mtime re-check would cover most of this.

findings.short_summary: Per-op holding dir + FS capability probe
findings.summary: claimEntry makes a holding directory and runs checkExclusivePublish (create, exclusive rename, two unlinks) for every single overwrite/delete, then renames in and out and removes the dir — roughly 8 metadata round trips per file where one unlink used to do.
findings.failure_scenario: A mirror run deleting 10k files on the SMB share does ~80k metadata round trips instead of ~10k. Probe the capability once per Tree (cache the result) and skip the probe on later claims.

findings.short_summary: Every Tree op re-walks path from root
findings.summary: Tree.directory/parent re-opens every path component from the root with openat for each Stat/Open/ReadDir/hash call, so each per-file operation costs O(depth) opens.
findings.failure_scenario: Over SMB, hashing a file 8 levels deep in ScanPaths/HashIfChanged costs ~9 network opens instead of 1; a full scan does depth-many opens per directory. Cache the directory fds during the walk or pass the parent fd down.

findings.short_summary: Inode identity check may fail on SMB
findings.summary: SameEntry compares dev/ino before vs after renaming the entry into the holding dir (RemoveFrom and checkObserved); on SMB mounts without stable server inode numbers, ino can change across rename.
findings.failure_scenario: On a cifs `noserverino` mount, or smbfs against a server without file-ID support, a rename into `.syncd-hold-*` yields a new ino → 'entry changed before removal' / ErrDestinationChanged on every remote delete and overwrite, deferred forever.

findings.short_summary: CheckCaseAliases runs twice per fast sync
findings.summary: runFastOnce calls CheckCaseAliases with the job-state baseline after ScanTrees (scanner.go:156) or scanPairForOpts (sync_once.go:456) has already run it on the same scans with a nil manifest.
findings.failure_scenario: Each fast sync folds and sorts every path in both trees twice. Pass the baseline into the scan-time check, or drop the scan-time one for the fast path.

content.text:
I reviewed [william-coronado/syncd#7](https://github.com/william-coronado/syncd/pull/7) and found 10 issues. These findings haven't been checked a second time, and none of them has been tested against the real NAS.

**Correctness, in order of severity:**

1. **A case-only rename can stop sync for good.** If you rename `Report.pdf` to `report.pdf`, or delete one and create the other, the case check sees a collision on every cycle. The manifest never gets updated, so it never clears. Renaming the remote copy doesn't fix it either. The only ways out are undoing the rename or deleting the manifest database.
2. **Holding folders on the shared remote break other machines' scans.** The new `.syncd-hold-*` folders are created inside the synced tree. The scanner fails on them before it applies the ignore rules. So if another machine scans the share while this one is mid-overwrite, its whole cycle fails. A holding folder left behind by a failed check after the new file is published stops every machine until someone deletes it by hand.
3. **Remote overwrites and deletes depend on an SMB feature that may be missing.** Every overwrite, every delete (remote deletes used to be a plain unlink) and every exclusive publish now needs no-replace renames or hard links on the destination. If the Synology mount supports neither, all of these fail.
4. **File timestamps are now set before the data is flushed.** The old code deliberately set the modified time after closing the file. On SMB or NFS, the flush can overwrite it with the current time. The fast `sync` would then re-copy the file every run, and `watch` would re-hash it every cycle.
5. **The inode check may fail on SMB.** Deletes and overwrites check that the file's inode number is unchanged after moving it into the holding folder. Some SMB mounts don't keep inode numbers stable across a rename, so these would be deferred every cycle.

**Performance and cleanup:**

6. Each `watch` change batch now loads every path in the manifest, which goes against the design of keeping that cost proportional to the batch.
7. An overwrite reads the destination file up to three times to hash it, and deletes now read every file in full first.
8. Every overwrite or delete creates a holding folder and re-tests what the filesystem supports. That's about 8 network round trips per file where one unlink used to do.
9. Each file operation re-opens every folder from the sync root down to the file.
10. The fast `sync` runs the case check twice on the same scan results.

## Filesystem safety

Symlinks and their descendants are excluded from reconciliation. File reads,
transfers, moves, deletions, and directory operations are confined to the
configured roots even if a parent is replaced by a symlink during a cycle.
Robust overwrites and deletes move the current entry into a private holding
directory before checking its identity, full modification timestamp, and
content hash. Transfers publish without replacing any new entry at the
destination name. A process that already has the old file open can still
write to that file after the check.

If a crash or concurrent recreation leaves a `.syncd-hold-...` directory,
sync pauses reconciliation there. Inspect and recover the retained file
before removing the holding directory and retrying. If the share supports
neither exclusive rename nor hard links, a guarded transfer reports an error.

Names that differ only by case, including directory components, stop the
cycle before any transfers or deletions. This applies on all filesystems so
pairs remain safe on case-insensitive APFS and SMB destinations. Resolve the
reported names on both sides before retrying; for a tracked case-only rename,
use an intermediate distinct name and sync it before the final rename.

input.new_string:
`.syncd-hold-...` directories are never reconciled. One that exists only
briefly is another syncd's operation in flight on a shared remote. One that
persists (after a crash or a concurrent recreation) holds a retained
original: every scan reports it as a scan issue in the log. Inspect and
recover the retained file, then remove the holding directory. If the share
supports neither exclusive rename nor hard links, publication falls back to
check-then-rename, so a name created by another writer in that brief window
can still be replaced.

Names that differ only by case, including directory components, stop the
cycle before any transfers or deletions. This applies on all filesystems so
pairs remain safe on case-insensitive APFS and SMB destinations. One case is
handled: `watch` (and `sync --hash`) propagate a case-only rename of a
tracked, unchanged file made on one side. On a case-insensitive destination
this can take two cycles. Otherwise, resolve the reported names by giving
them distinct names, or the same spelling on both sides, before retrying.
A directory case rename needs the same rename made on the other side.

findings.short_summary: Case-only rename permanently wedges sync
findings.summary: CheckCaseAliases folds manifest/baseline paths together with both scans, so a case-only rename (or deleting `Foo` and creating `foo`) is refused before planning, and because the manifest is never updated the refusal repeats forever.
findings.failure_scenario: User renames `Report.pdf` → `report.pdf` locally. Manifest holds `Report.pdf`, local scan has `report.pdf`, remote still has `Report.pdf` → `case-insensitive path collision` on every cycle; the only escape is reverting the rename or deleting the manifest DB.

findings.short_summary: Holding dirs abort other clients' scans
findings.summary: Transient `.syncd-hold-*` directories are created inside the synced tree (including on the shared remote), and the scanner hard-fails on them before the ignore matcher runs, so any concurrent scan by another machine — or any leftover from a failed post-publish check — aborts the whole cycle.
findings.failure_scenario: Machine B's remote poll walks the share while machine A is mid-overwrite → `unfinished sync operation` → whole RunRobustOnce fails; a leftover holding dir stalls every client until manual cleanup.

findings.short_summary: Overwrites/deletes need RENAME_EXCL or hard links
findings.summary: Every robust overwrite, every delete (including network deletes that used to be a plain unlink), and every exclusive publish now requires the destination FS to support RENAME_EXCL/RENAME_NOREPLACE or hard links; on mounts with neither, all such operations fail.
findings.failure_scenario: On an SMB mount without exclusive rename or hard links, checkExclusivePublish fails → remote deletes, overwrites and new uploads all stop.

findings.short_summary: mtime now set before fsync/close
findings.summary: The preserved mtime is applied before `tmp.Sync()`/`tmp.Close()`, whereas the old code deliberately set it after closing; on network filesystems, cached writes flushed at fsync/close can bump the mtime to 'now'.
findings.failure_scenario: Download/upload to smbfs or NFS: buffered data flushed after utimes resets last-write time, so fast sync re-copies forever and robust HashIfChanged re-hashes every cycle.

findings.short_summary: Scoped cycle loads full manifest names per batch
findings.summary: RunRobustScoped now calls `Repo.LoadNames` (a full `file_manifest` table scan) and `dirRepo.LoadAll` on every fsnotify batch, and CheckScopedCaseAliases walks every baseline name and its ancestors.
findings.failure_scenario: A 500k-file tree: every single-file save loads 500k paths from SQLite before reconciling one path.

findings.short_summary: Destination re-hashed up to 3× per action
findings.summary: checkObserved hashes the full destination content on every call, and copyBetween calls it up to three times per overwrite; deletes also fully read each target, and the EXDEV trash path hashes 3–4×.
findings.failure_scenario: Overwriting a 2 GB file on the NAS reads it 3 times over SMB before the new copy lands.

findings.short_summary: Per-op holding dir + FS capability probe
findings.summary: claimEntry makes a holding directory and runs checkExclusivePublish for every single overwrite/delete — roughly 8 metadata round trips per file where one unlink used to do.
findings.failure_scenario: A mirror run deleting 10k files on the SMB share does ~80k metadata round trips instead of ~10k.

findings.short_summary: Every Tree op re-walks path from root
findings.summary: Tree.directory/parent re-opens every path component from the root with openat for each Stat/Open/ReadDir/hash call.
findings.failure_scenario: Over SMB, hashing a file 8 levels deep costs ~9 network opens instead of 1.

findings.short_summary: Inode identity check may fail on SMB
findings.summary: SameEntry compares dev/ino before vs after renaming the entry into the holding dir; on SMB mounts without stable server inode numbers, ino can change across rename.
findings.failure_scenario: On a cifs `noserverino` mount, every remote delete and overwrite is deferred forever.

findings.short_summary: CheckCaseAliases runs twice per fast sync
findings.summary: runFastOnce calls CheckCaseAliases with the job-state baseline after ScanTrees or scanPairForOpts has already run it on the same scans.
findings.failure_scenario: Each fast sync folds and sorts every path in both trees twice.

findings.short_summary: Case-only rename permanently wedges sync
findings.summary: CheckCaseAliases folds manifest/baseline paths together with both scans, so a case-only rename (or deleting `Foo` and creating `foo`) is refused before planning, and because the manifest is never updated the refusal repeats forever.
findings.failure_scenario: User renames `Report.pdf` → `report.pdf` locally. Manifest holds `Report.pdf`, local scan has `report.pdf`, remote still has `Report.pdf` → `case-insensitive path collision` on every cycle; the only escape is reverting the rename or deleting the manifest DB.

findings.short_summary: Holding dirs abort other clients' scans
findings.summary: Transient `.syncd-hold-*` directories are created inside the synced tree (including on the shared remote), and the scanner hard-fails on them before the ignore matcher runs, so any concurrent scan by another machine — or any leftover from a failed post-publish check — aborts the whole cycle.
findings.failure_scenario: Machine B's remote poll walks the share while machine A is mid-overwrite → `unfinished sync operation` → whole RunRobustOnce fails; a leftover holding dir stalls every client until manual cleanup.

findings.short_summary: Overwrites/deletes need RENAME_EXCL or hard links
findings.summary: Every robust overwrite, every delete (including network deletes that used to be a plain unlink), and every exclusive publish now requires the destination FS to support RENAME_EXCL/RENAME_NOREPLACE or hard links; on mounts with neither, all such operations fail.
findings.failure_scenario: On an SMB mount without exclusive rename or hard links, checkExclusivePublish fails → remote deletes, overwrites and new uploads all stop.

findings.short_summary: mtime now set before fsync/close
findings.summary: The preserved mtime is applied before `tmp.Sync()`/`tmp.Close()`, whereas the old code deliberately set it after closing; on network filesystems, cached writes flushed at fsync/close can bump the mtime to 'now'.
findings.failure_scenario: Download/upload to smbfs or NFS: buffered data flushed after utimes resets last-write time, so fast sync re-copies forever and robust HashIfChanged re-hashes every cycle.

findings.short_summary: Scoped cycle loads full manifest names per batch
findings.summary: RunRobustScoped now calls `Repo.LoadNames` (a full `file_manifest` table scan) and `dirRepo.LoadAll` on every fsnotify batch, and CheckScopedCaseAliases walks every baseline name and its ancestors.
findings.failure_scenario: A 500k-file tree: every single-file save loads 500k paths from SQLite before reconciling one path.

findings.short_summary: Destination re-hashed up to 3× per action
findings.summary: checkObserved hashes the full destination content on every call, and copyBetween calls it up to three times per overwrite; deletes also fully read each target, and the EXDEV trash path hashes 3–4×.
findings.failure_scenario: Overwriting a 2 GB file on the NAS reads it 3 times over SMB before the new copy lands.

findings.short_summary: Per-op holding dir + FS capability probe
findings.summary: claimEntry makes a holding directory and runs checkExclusivePublish for every single overwrite/delete — roughly 8 metadata round trips per file where one unlink used to do.
findings.failure_scenario: A mirror run deleting 10k files on the SMB share does ~80k metadata round trips instead of ~10k.

findings.short_summary: Every Tree op re-walks path from root
findings.summary: Tree.directory/parent re-opens every path component from the root with openat for each Stat/Open/ReadDir/hash call.
findings.failure_scenario: Over SMB, hashing a file 8 levels deep costs ~9 network opens instead of 1.

findings.short_summary: Inode identity check may fail on SMB
findings.summary: SameEntry compares dev/ino before vs after renaming the entry into the holding dir; on SMB mounts without stable server inode numbers, ino can change across rename.
findings.failure_scenario: On a cifs `noserverino` mount, every remote delete and overwrite is deferred forever.

findings.short_summary: CheckCaseAliases runs twice per fast sync
findings.summary: runFastOnce calls CheckCaseAliases with the job-state baseline after ScanTrees or scanPairForOpts has already run it on the same scans.
findings.failure_scenario: Each fast sync folds and sorts every path in both trees twice.

content.text:
I fixed the top 4 findings on `codex/fix-sync-safety`. Build, vet, the full test suite, `-race` and both cross-builds pass on this Mac. Nothing is committed yet.

1. **A case-only rename no longer stops sync for good** ([aliases.go](internal/fs/aliases.go)).
   - Only names that actually exist on a side are compared now. A manifest spelling that's gone from both sides no longer blocks the pair, so renaming both sides the same way clears a collision.
   - One case now goes through: a file renamed by case on one side, where the other side still has the old spelling with unchanged content (checked by hash). The planner turns it into a delete of the old name and a create of the new one. On a case-insensitive destination this can take two cycles.
   - The fast `sync` keeps no hashes, so it never gets this exception and stays strict as before.
   - In `watch`, the per-batch check can't tell a rename from a real collision, so when it trips it now runs a full cycle ([sync_loop.go](internal/app/sync_loop.go)). The full cycle either passes the rename on or refuses with the same error.
   - Real collisions are still refused: two spellings on one side, a folder renamed by case, or a renamed file whose old copy was edited.
2. **Holding folders no longer abort scans** ([scanner.go](internal/fs/scanner.go)). The scanner skips them and logs a warning every scan, so a kept original isn't forgotten. The per-batch case check in `watch` now skips them too.
3. **Mounts without no-replace renames or hard links now work** ([claim.go](internal/fs/claim.go)). When neither is available, syncd checks that the destination name is free and then does a plain rename. This is no worse than before the PR: another writer creating that name in that short gap can still be overwritten. I also removed the per-operation probe that tested for these features.
4. **The file's modified time is set after the data is flushed and the file closed** ([atomic_copy.go](internal/fs/atomic_copy.go)), as the old code did.

**Tests:** I added tests for the rename exception and its refusals, the `watch` rename going through, a real collision still refused, a scan skipping a holding folder, and writes and deletes on a mount without either feature. Two existing tests pinned the old behavior, so I rewrote them: one expected a scan to stop on a holding folder, the other expected a case-only rename to be refused. I also updated the "Filesystem safety" section of the README.

**Not tested:**
- The two-cycle rename test ran on this Mac's disk; Linux, where names are case-sensitive, wasn't tested.
- Neither the new fallback nor the timestamp order has been tried on the actual Synology share. The fallback is only tested by faking the missing features.

The other six findings, all performance or cleanup apart from the inode check on SMB, are left as they were.

fix: unwedge case-only renames and keep SMB writes working

Address the top findings from the PR #7 review:

- Case aliases: compare only names present on a side, so a stale
  baseline spelling no longer blocks a pair forever. Allow a hashed,
  unchanged file's case-only rename on one side (the planner turns it
  into delete + create; exclusive publish and observed-entry checks keep
  the two from touching one file). The fast path, which has no hashes,
  stays strict. Scoped cycles escalate an ErrCaseAlias to a full cycle,
  which can tell a rename from a genuine collision.
- Holding directories: scans skip .syncd-hold-* and report a scan
  issue instead of aborting, so another client's in-flight operation on
  a shared remote no longer fails every other client's cycle.
- Publication: when a mount supports neither exclusive rename nor hard
  links, fall back to check-then-rename instead of refusing every
  overwrite and delete. Drop the per-operation capability probe.
- Atomic copy: set the preserved mtime after fsync and close, as before,
  so a late network flush cannot overwrite it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -3 && git status --short

Run a fast, size+mtime-based sync job (mirror, update, or two-way).

Either pass --left and --right for a one-off job, or omit them to run every
job listed in the config file (~/.syncd.yaml by default, or --config); use
--job to run just one named job from that file. Pass --hash to use the
robust, hash-based engine instead of the fast reconciler for this run.

Usage:
  syncd sync [flags]

Flags:
      --config string       Config file (default $HOME/.syncd.yaml)
      --dry-run             Print the sync summary and exit without changing anything or persisting job state (does not require --yes). Still takes the per-job lock and opens the state database.
      --hash                Use the robust hash-based engine instead of the fast size+mtime reconciler
  -h, --help                help for sync
      --job string          Run only this named job from the config file
      --left string         Left folder path (one-off job; requires --right)
      --max-delete string   Most files one unattended run may delete from either side: a count (100), a percentage of the files there (50%; never trips on 10 or fewer), or off; applies with --yes (the confirm prompt is the gate otherwise) (default "50%")
      --mode string         Sync mode for a one-off job: mirror, update, two-way (default "mirror")
      --no-trash            Delete files outright instead of moving those on a local disk to <state-dir>/trash
      --right string        Right folder path (one-off job; requires --left)
      --trash-days int      Days to keep trashed files (0 keeps them forever) (default 30)
      --yes                 Skip the interactive confirmation prompt

content.text:
I tested against the share, and every check passed. I didn't touch your real `~/dev` or the rest of `/Volumes/dev`: everything ran in a temporary folder, `/Volumes/dev/.syncd-review-probe.tmp`, which I've since deleted. Its `.tmp` name is in syncd's built-in ignore list, so a running watch daemon wouldn't have synced it.

**What this share supports:**
- **No-replace rename and hard links:** neither is supported on your Synology mount ("operation not supported"). So the PR as originally pushed would have failed every overwrite, every delete and every new upload to the NAS; finding 3 was a real bug on your setup. With the fix, an upload onto an existing name is refused and an upload onto a free name succeeds.
- **File names are case-insensitive:** looking up `case.txt` finds `Case.txt`.
- **Inode numbers stay the same across a rename,** so the identity check works here, and finding 9 doesn't apply on this mount.
- **File times keep 100 ns precision.** A copy's timestamp matched its source to that precision with the new "set the time after closing" order.

**End to end with `syncd sync --hash --mode two-way`** (local side in my scratchpad, remote side on the share):

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Initial push of 3 files | Synced |
| Local rename `Report.txt` → `report.txt` | Reached the share in one cycle, with no stray old spelling |
| Overwrite of an existing file | Remote content updated |
| Local delete | Removed on the share |
| Rename on the share `report.txt` → `REPORT.txt` | Pulled back in one cycle; content intact |
| Run again with no changes | Nothing to do |

No `.syncd-hold-*` folders were left behind on either side.

**Cleanup:** I deleted the probe folder on the share, my scratch copy, the throwaway probe test, and the state files and trash entry the test created. `~/.local/state/syncd` is back to how it was. The repo has no new changes to commit.

I also saved a note on what this mount supports, plus the safe way to test against it, so later sessions don't have to work it out again.

file.content:
Symlinks and their descendants are excluded from reconciliation. File reads,
transfers, moves, deletions, and directory operations are confined to the
configured roots even if a parent is replaced by a symlink during a cycle.
Robust overwrites and deletes move the current entry into a private holding
directory before checking its identity, full modification timestamp, and
content hash. Transfers publish without replacing any new entry at the
destination name. A process that already has the old file open can still
write to that file after the check.

`.syncd-hold-...` directories are never reconciled. One that exists only
briefly is another syncd's operation in flight on a shared remote. One that
persists (after a crash or a concurrent recreation) holds a retained
original: every scan reports it as a scan issue in the log. Inspect and
recover the retained file, then remove the holding directory. If the share
supports neither exclusive rename nor hard links, publication falls back to
check-then-rename, so a name created by another writer in that brief window
can still be replaced.

findings.short_summary: Case-only rename permanently wedges sync
findings.summary: CheckCaseAliases folds manifest/baseline paths together with both scans, so a case-only rename is refused before planning and the refusal repeats forever.
findings.failure_scenario: User renames `Report.pdf` → `report.pdf` locally; every cycle refuses with a case collision until the rename is reverted or the manifest DB deleted.

findings.short_summary: Holding dirs abort other clients' scans
findings.summary: Transient `.syncd-hold-*` entries on the shared remote made the scanner hard-fail, aborting other machines' cycles.
findings.failure_scenario: Machine B's remote poll runs while machine A is mid-overwrite on the NAS → whole cycle fails with `unfinished sync operation`.

findings.short_summary: Overwrites/deletes need RENAME_EXCL or hard links
findings.summary: Every overwrite, delete and exclusive publish required RENAME_EXCL or hard links on the destination FS.
findings.failure_scenario: On the user's Synology smbfs mount both return ENOTSUP, so all remote writes and deletes would fail.

findings.short_summary: mtime now set before fsync/close
findings.summary: The preserved mtime was applied before fsync/close, so a late network flush could overwrite it.
findings.failure_scenario: Upload to smbfs/NFS: the flush after utimes stamps 'now', so fast sync re-copies and HashIfChanged re-hashes forever.

findings.short_summary: Scoped cycle loads full manifest names per batch
findings.summary: RunRobustScoped called `Repo.LoadNames` (full table scan) and `dirRepo.LoadAll` on every fsnotify batch, and CheckScopedCaseAliases walked every baseline name.
findings.failure_scenario: A 500k-file tree: every single-file save loads 500k paths from SQLite before reconciling one path.

findings.short_summary: Destination re-hashed up to 3× per action
findings.summary: checkObserved hashed the full destination on every call (up to 3× per overwrite), and the EXDEV trash path hashed 3–4×.
findings.failure_scenario: Overwriting a 2 GB file on the NAS read it 3 times over SMB before the new copy landed.

findings.short_summary: Per-op holding dir + FS capability probe
findings.summary: claimEntry made a holding directory and probed FS capabilities for every overwrite/delete — ~8 metadata round trips per file.
findings.failure_scenario: A mirror run deleting 10k files on the SMB share did ~80k metadata round trips instead of ~10k.

findings.short_summary: Every Tree op re-walks path from root
findings.summary: Tree.directory/parent re-opened every path component from the root for each Stat/Open/ReadDir/hash call.
findings.failure_scenario: Over SMB, hashing a file 8 levels deep cost ~9 network opens instead of 1; a full scan did depth-many opens per directory.

findings.short_summary: Inode identity check may fail on SMB
findings.summary: SameEntry compares dev/ino across the claim rename; on SMB mounts without stable server inode numbers, ino can change across rename.
findings.failure_scenario: On a cifs `noserverino` mount every remote delete and overwrite would be deferred forever (measured stable on the user's Synology smbfs mount).

findings.short_summary: CheckCaseAliases runs twice per fast sync
findings.summary: runFastOnce re-ran CheckCaseAliases with the job-state baseline after the scan had already run it.
findings.failure_scenario: Each fast sync folded and sorted every path in both trees twice.

content.text:
I fixed all five remaining performance findings on `codex/fix-sync-safety`. Build, vet, tests, `-race` and both cross-builds pass, and the same end-to-end scenario still works on your share. Nothing is committed yet.

**What changed:**
- **`watch` no longer loads the whole manifest for each batch of changes** ([sync_loop.go](internal/app/sync_loop.go), [aliases.go](internal/fs/aliases.go)). It now only lists the folders the changed files are in, on both sides, which already shows every spelling that exists there. The folder baseline is loaded again only when a batch contains a folder, as before the PR.
- **Each overwrite or delete reads the destination file's content once** ([worker_pool.go](internal/execute/worker_pool.go)). The first check hashes it. Later re-checks compare only identity, size and full-precision modified time, which any write through an already-open file changes. The cross-disk trash copy no longer hashes the file three times; it compares the file's metadata before and after copying.
- **No temporary folder per operation** ([claim.go](internal/fs/claim.go)). The file is now renamed to a hidden `.syncd-hold-…` name beside it, which takes one metadata operation instead of four. Once a disk turns out to lack both no-replace rename and hard links, syncd stops trying them there, which saves two failed network calls per operation on your share.
- **Scans no longer re-open every folder from the root** ([scan_fs.go](internal/fs/scan_fs.go)). A full scan keeps the folders on its current path open and reaches files and subfolders through them. Each step still refuses to follow symlinks. The `watch` per-change scan also stats and hashes a file from a single opened parent folder.
- **The fast `sync` runs the case check once.** The second run could never change the result.

Tests cover each of these. I updated one existing test for the new hidden-file layout, and updated the README.

**Measured on your share**, against the previous commit:

| | Previous commit | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Hashed scan of 288 files in 113 folders, cold cache | 6.07 s | 4.96 s |
| Same scan, warm cache | 3.52 s | 3.58 s |
| 100 MB remote overwrite | 3.63 s | 3.28 s |

The gains are smaller than the finding suggested. macOS's SMB client caches folder lookups and file data, so repeated opens and reads are often served locally. They should matter more on large cold trees, on files bigger than that cache, and on the `watch` per-batch manifest load, which grows with the size of the tree.

**Not done:**
- Copy, move and delete operations still re-open folders from the root each time, on purpose. That is what catches a parent folder being swapped out in the middle of a cycle.
- Finding 9 (the inode check) is left as is. Inode numbers are stable on your mount, though other SMB setups may differ.

**Please delete this folder yourself:** `/Volumes/dev/.syncd-review-probe.tmp` (202 MB of test data). A safety check blocks me from removing a top-level folder on a mounted drive. Everything else is cleaned up, and `~/.local/state/syncd` is back to how it was.

```bash
rm -rf /Volumes/dev/.syncd-review-probe.tmp
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# deploy-syncd.sh - build syncd for this Mac and for linux/amd64, install
# both, and restart any syncd watch service that is running, so it picks up
# the new binary.
#
# Usage: ~/deploy-syncd.sh [--local-only | --remote-only] [--no-restart] [--test]
#
#   --local-only    build and install on this Mac only
#   --remote-only   build and install on the Linux host only
#   --no-restart    install the binaries, but leave running services alone
#   --test          run `go vet` and `go test` before building
#
# Overridable with environment variables:
#   SYNCD_REPO       source checkout   (default: ~/dev/tools/syncd)
#   SYNCD_REMOTE     ssh destination   (default: william@192.168.50.44)
#   SYNCD_REMOTE_BIN remote bin dir    (default: /home/william/.local/bin)
#
# Why a restart: a running `syncd watch` keeps executing the binary it was
# started from. Replacing the file does not change the running process; it
# only picks up the new code when the service restarts. Uninstalling and
# reinstalling is NOT needed - the launchd plist / systemd unit only names
# the binary's path and its watch flags. Re-run `syncd service install`
# only to change those flags.

set -euo pipefail

REPO="${SYNCD_REPO:-$HOME/dev/tools/syncd}"
LOCAL_BIN_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin"
REMOTE="${SYNCD_REMOTE:-william@192.168.50.44}"
REMOTE_BIN_DIR="${SYNCD_REMOTE_BIN:-/home/william/.local/bin}"

do_local=1
do_remote=1
restart=1
run_tests=0

for arg in "$@"; do
	case "$arg" in
	--local-only) do_remote=0 ;;
	--remote-only) do_local=0 ;;
	--no-restart) restart=0 ;;
	--test) run_tests=1 ;;
	-h | --help)
		sed -n '2,24p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
		exit 0
		;;
	*)
		echo "unknown option: $arg (see --help)" >&2
		exit 2
		;;
	esac
done
if [[ $do_local -eq 0 && $do_remote -eq 0 ]]; then
	echo "--local-only and --remote-only together leave nothing to do" >&2
	exit 2
fi

step() { printf '\n==> %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf 'warning: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

[[ -f "$REPO/go.mod" ]] || {
	echo "not a syncd checkout: $REPO (set SYNCD_REPO)" >&2
	exit 1
}

# --- what is being deployed -------------------------------------------------
rev="$(git -C "$REPO" describe --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
branch="$(git -C "$REPO" branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || true)"
step "Deploying syncd ${rev} (branch: ${branch:-detached})"
[[ "$rev" == *-dirty ]] && warn "the checkout has uncommitted changes; they are included in this build"
[[ -n "$branch" && "$branch" != "main" ]] && warn "building from '$branch', not main"

if [[ $run_tests -eq 1 ]]; then
	step "Vetting and testing"
	(cd "$REPO" && go vet ./... && go test ./...)
fi

# --- build -------------------------------------------------------------------
build_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$build_dir"' EXIT

if [[ $do_local -eq 1 ]]; then
	step "Building for this machine ($(go env GOOS)/$(go env GOARCH))"
	(cd "$REPO" && go build -trimpath -o "$build_dir/syncd-local" ./cmd/syncd)
fi
if [[ $do_remote -eq 1 ]]; then
	step "Building for linux/amd64"
	# modernc.org/sqlite is pure Go, so this is a static, cgo-free binary.
	(cd "$REPO" && GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -o "$build_dir/syncd-linux-amd64" ./cmd/syncd)
fi

# --- install locally ---------------------------------------------------------
# Copy beside the target, then rename over it. Overwriting a running
# executable in place can get the running process killed on macOS (its
# code signature no longer matches), and fails with "Text file busy" on
# Linux. A rename swaps in a new file; the running process keeps the old one
# until it restarts.
if [[ $do_local -eq 1 ]]; then
	step "Installing to $LOCAL_BIN_DIR/syncd"
	mkdir -p "$LOCAL_BIN_DIR"
	cp "$build_dir/syncd-local" "$LOCAL_BIN_DIR/.syncd.new"
	chmod +x "$LOCAL_BIN_DIR/.syncd.new"
	mv -f "$LOCAL_BIN_DIR/.syncd.new" "$LOCAL_BIN_DIR/syncd"
	echo "installed: $(shasum -a 256 "$LOCAL_BIN_DIR/syncd" | cut -c1-16)…"

	if [[ $restart -eq 1 ]]; then
		step "Restarting running launchd services"
		deployed="$(cd "$LOCAL_BIN_DIR" && pwd -P)/syncd"
		found=0
		shopt -s nullglob
		for plist in "$HOME"/Library/LaunchAgents/com.syncd.watch*.plist; do
			found=1
			label="$(basename "$plist" .plist)"
			target="gui/$(id -u)/$label"
			bin="$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Print :ProgramArguments:0' "$plist" 2>/dev/null || true)"
			if [[ "$bin" != "$deployed" ]]; then
				warn "$label runs $bin, not $deployed; leaving it alone"
			elif launchctl print "$target" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
				launchctl kickstart -k "$target"
				echo "restarted $label"
			else
				echo "$label is installed but not loaded; it will use the new binary when started"
			fi
		done
		shopt -u nullglob
		[[ $found -eq 1 ]] || echo "no syncd launchd service installed"
	fi
fi

# --- install on the Linux host ----------------------------------------------
if [[ $do_remote -eq 1 ]]; then
	step "Installing to $REMOTE:$REMOTE_BIN_DIR/syncd"
	# One shared ssh connection for every step: authenticate once.
	ctl="$build_dir/ssh-ctl"
	ssh_opts=(-o ControlMaster=auto -o "ControlPath=$ctl" -o ControlPersist=60 -o ConnectTimeout=10)
	trap 'ssh "${ssh_opts[@]}" -O exit "$REMOTE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; rm -rf "$build_dir"' EXIT

	ssh "${ssh_opts[@]}" "$REMOTE" "mkdir -p '$REMOTE_BIN_DIR'"
	scp -q "${ssh_opts[@]}" "$build_dir/syncd-linux-amd64" "$REMOTE:$REMOTE_BIN_DIR/.syncd.new"
	want="$(shasum -a 256 "$build_dir/syncd-linux-amd64" | cut -d' ' -f1)"

	ssh "${ssh_opts[@]}" "$REMOTE" bash -s -- "$REMOTE_BIN_DIR" "$want" "$restart" <<'REMOTE_SCRIPT'
set -euo pipefail
bin_dir="$1" want="$2" restart="$3"
new="$bin_dir/.syncd.new"
got="$(sha256sum "$new" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
if [[ "$got" != "$want" ]]; then
	rm -f "$new"
	echo "checksum mismatch after copy; nothing installed" >&2
	exit 1
fi
chmod +x "$new"
mv -f "$new" "$bin_dir/syncd"
echo "installed: ${got:0:16}…"

[[ "$restart" == 1 ]] || exit 0
printf '\n==> Restarting running systemd user services\n'
deployed="$(cd "$bin_dir" && pwd -P)/syncd"
units="$(systemctl --user list-unit-files 'syncd-watch*' --no-legend 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"
if [[ -z "$units" ]]; then
	echo "no syncd systemd service installed"
	exit 0
fi
for unit in $units; do
	exec_bin="$(systemctl --user show -p ExecStart --value "$unit" | sed -n 's/.*path=\([^ ;]*\).*/\1/p')"
	if [[ "$exec_bin" != "$deployed" ]]; then
		echo "warning: $unit runs $exec_bin, not $deployed; leaving it alone" >&2
	elif systemctl --user is-active --quiet "$unit"; then
		systemctl --user restart "$unit"
		sleep 2
		if systemctl --user is-active --quiet "$unit"; then
			echo "restarted $unit (active)"
		else
			echo "warning: $unit is not active after restart:" >&2
			systemctl --user status "$unit" --no-pager -n 10 >&2 || true
			exit 1
		fi
	else
		echo "$unit is installed but not running; it will use the new binary when started"
	fi
done
REMOTE_SCRIPT
fi

step "Done: syncd ${rev}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# deploy-syncd.sh - build syncd for this Mac and for linux/amd64, install
# both, and restart any syncd watch service that is running, so it picks up

#
# Usage: ~/deploy-syncd.sh [--local-only | --remote-only] [--no-restart] [--test]
#
#   --local-only    build and install on this Mac only
#   --remote-only   build and install on the Linux host only
#   --no-restart    install the binaries, but leave running services alone
#   --test          run `go vet` and `go test` before building

# Overridable with environment variables:
#   SYNCD_REPO       source checkout   (default: ~/dev/tools/syncd)
#   SYNCD_REMOTE     ssh destination   (default: william@192.168.50.44)
#   SYNCD_REMOTE_BIN remote bin dir    (default: /home/william/.local/bin)
#

# started from. Replacing the file does not change the running process; it
# only picks up the new code when the service restarts. Uninstalling and
# reinstalling is NOT needed - the launchd plist / systemd unit only names
# the binary's path and its watch flags. Re-run `syncd service install`
# only to change those flags.

set -euo pipefail

REPO="${SYNCD_REPO:-$HOME/dev/tools/syncd}"
LOCAL_BIN_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin"
REMOTE="${SYNCD_REMOTE:-william@192.168.50.44}"
REMOTE_BIN_DIR="${SYNCD_REMOTE_BIN:-/home/william/.local/bin}"

do_local=1
do_remote=1
restart=1
run_tests=0

for arg in "$@"; do
	case "$arg" in
	--local-only) do_remote=0 ;;
	--remote-only) do_local=0 ;;
	--no-restart) restart=0 ;;
	--test) run_tests=1 ;;
	-h | --help)
		sed -n '2,24p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
		exit 0
		;;
	*)
		echo "unknown option: $arg (see --help)" >&2
		exit 2
		;;
	esac
done
if [[ $do_local -eq 0 && $do_remote -eq 0 ]]; then
	echo "--local-only and --remote-only together leave nothing to do" >&2
	exit 2
fi

step() { printf '\n==> %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf 'warning: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

[[ -f "$REPO/go.mod" ]] || {
	echo "not a syncd checkout: $REPO (set SYNCD_REPO)" >&2
	exit 1
}

# --- what is being deployed -------------------------------------------------
rev="$(git -C "$REPO" describe --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
branch="$(git -C "$REPO" branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || true)"

new="$bin_dir/.syncd.new"
got="$(sha256sum "$new" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
if [[ "$got" != "$want" ]]; then
	rm -f "$new"
	echo "checksum mismatch after copy; nothing installed" >&2
	exit 1
fi
chmod +x "$new"
mv -f "$new" "$bin_dir/syncd"
echo "installed: ${got:0:16}…"

[[ "$restart" == 1 ]] || exit 0
printf '\n==> Restarting running systemd user services\n'
deployed="$(cd "$bin_dir" && pwd -P)/syncd"
units="$(systemctl --user list-unit-files 'syncd-watch*' --no-legend 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"

**On your question:** yes, you need a restart, but not an uninstall or reinstall. A running `syncd watch` keeps using the binary it started from, even after the file on disk is replaced. The launchd plist or systemd unit only records the binary's path and the watch options. So a plain restart picks up the new code, and the script does it for you. You'd only re-run `syncd service install` to change those watch options.

Your Linux host does need this: `syncd-watch.service` is enabled and running from `/home/william/.local/bin/syncd`. No service is installed on this Mac.

The rename matters. Overwriting a running program in place can get it killed on macOS, and fails with "Text file busy" on Linux. A rename swaps the file safely while the old process keeps running until its restart.

**Options:** `--local-only`, `--remote-only`, `--no-restart`, and `--test` (runs `go vet` and `go test` first). It also warns if the checkout has uncommitted changes or isn't on `main`.

**Checked without changing anything:** the syntax and option handling, that the Linux build comes out as a standalone x86-64 binary, and that on the remote host the script finds `syncd-watch.service` running the deployed path.

I haven't run a real deploy, because it would replace the binary and restart the daemon on your Linux host. To run it yourself:

I updated the Git section of `CLAUDE.md`. It replaces the outdated text, which said there was no remote and that a `feat/syncd` branch might exist. It now says:

- `main` is the only long-lived branch and the default, and it tracks `origin` (`github.com/william-coronado/syncd`).
- Work goes on a short-lived branch off `main` and lands through a GitHub PR merged with a merge commit, not squash. That matches how PRs 4–7 were merged.
- After merging, delete the branch locally and on GitHub. GitHub won't do it automatically, because "delete branch on merge" is off for this repo.
- The `Co-Authored-By` line is unchanged.

The change isn't committed yet. The new section says work should go through a PR, so I'm checking with you rather than committing straight to `main`.

**Something I found, not from my work:** there's an untracked file in the repo root, `syncd_conflict_20261115_014056`. It's an older Mac build of the `syncd` binary from Nov 14. Your `~/dev` is mirrored to `/Volumes/dev`, and the same file is there too. So it's most likely the conflict copy a two-way sync made when the git-ignored `syncd` binary differed on the two sides. The fast two-way mode keeps the newer file and renames the older one. `.gitignore` covers `/syncd` but not its conflict copies, which is why it shows up as untracked. I didn't touch it. If you don't need it, delete it here and on the share. To keep it from happening again, you could add `tools/syncd/syncd` to `~/dev/.syncdignore` so the build output isn't synced at all.
